51.solution: Serine is a hydroxy-amino acid. Its side chain \((R)\) group is the hydroxymethyl group \(\text{HO}-\text{CH}_2-\) (structure \(\text{HOCH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)-\text{COOH}\)). Option A \((\text{CH}_3-)\) is alanine, option C \((\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-)\) is valine, and option B is the side chain of threonine.

52.solution: A triglyceride is a triester of glycerol with three fatty acids, so it has three ester linkages. Complete hydrolysis of one triester needs \(3\) molecules of water (one per ester bond) to give glycerol \(+\) 3 fatty acids. Therefore \(n\) mol triglyceride requires \(3n\) mol \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\).

53.subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
53.solution: By Fajans' rules, covalent character increases with a small cation and a large anion (greater polarising power / greater polarisability). \(\text{Li}^{+}\) is the smallest group-1 cation and \(\text{I}^{-}\) is the largest group-17 anion, so \(\text{LiI}\) has the maximum covalent character among the given ionic compounds.

54.subtopic: Van't Hoff Factor and Abnormal Molar Mass
54.solution: \(\Delta T_f = i \times K_f \times m\). So \(i = \dfrac{\Delta T_f}{K_f \times m} = \dfrac{0.046}{1.86 \times 0.02} = \dfrac{0.046}{0.0372} = 1.236\). For a solute giving \(n=2\) ions, \(\alpha = \dfrac{i-1}{n-1} = \dfrac{1.236-1}{2-1} = 0.236\). Percent dissociation \(= 0.236 \times 100 = 23.6\%\).

55.subtopic: Rate of Reaction, Stoichiometry and Average Rate
55.solution: For \(\text{NO}_2 + \text{CO} \to \text{NO} + \text{CO}_2\) all stoichiometric coefficients are 1, so the single rate is \(-\dfrac{\Delta[\text{CO}]}{\Delta t} = -\dfrac{\Delta[\text{NO}_2]}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{\Delta[\text{NO}]}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{\Delta[\text{CO}_2]}{\Delta t}\). Given rate of formation of \(\text{NO} = Y\), the rate of disappearance of \(\text{CO}\) is also \(Y\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}\,\text{s}^{-1}\).

56.subtopic: Side-Chain Reactions, Oxidation and Other Transformations
56.solution: Toluene treated with chromyl chloride \((\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2)\) in \(\text{CS}_2\) forms a brown chromium complex which on hydrolysis gives benzaldehyde. This is the Etard reaction, a controlled oxidation of the methyl side chain to \(-\text{CHO}\) (not to \(-\text{COOH}\)).

57.subtopic: Chemical Reactions and Basicity of Amines
57.solution: Lower \(pK_b\) means stronger base. Aromatic amines (benzenamine/aniline) are weak because the lone pair is delocalised into the ring. Aliphatic amines are stronger than \(\text{NH}_3\). Among aliphatic amines a secondary amine is a stronger base than a primary one. N-Methylethanamine \((\text{CH}_3\text{NHCH}_2\text{CH}_3)\) is a secondary aliphatic amine, hence the strongest base and the lowest \(pK_b\).

58.solution: The structure shown is ethanol, \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}\), with molecular formula \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}\). Molar mass \(= (2\times 12) + (6\times 1) + (1\times 16) = 24 + 6 + 16 = 46\ \text{g mol}^{-1}\).
58.note: Stem image (ethanol, CH3CH2OH) read and confirmed.

59.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
59.solution: By the Nernst equation, \(E_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{cell} - \dfrac{0.0592}{n}\log\dfrac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Ag}^{+}]^{2}}\) with \(n=2\). Given \(E_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{cell} - 0.0592\), so \(\dfrac{0.0592}{2}\log\dfrac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Ag}^{+}]^{2}} = 0.0592\), giving \(\log\dfrac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Ag}^{+}]^{2}} = 2\), i.e. \(\dfrac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Ag}^{+}]^{2}} = 100\). For \([\text{Zn}^{2+}]=1\,M\) and \([\text{Ag}^{+}]=0.1\,M\): \(\dfrac{1}{(0.1)^2}=100\). Option A satisfies this.

60.subtopic: Unit Cells, Edge Length and Atomic Radius
60.solution: For an fcc unit cell the atoms touch along the face diagonal, so \(a = 2\sqrt{2}\,r\). With \(r = 141.4\ \text{pm} = 141.4\times 10^{-10}\ \text{cm}\): \(a = 2\sqrt{2}\times 141.4\times 10^{-10} \approx 4.0\times 10^{-8}\ \text{cm}\) (since \(141.4 \approx 100\sqrt{2}\)). Volume \(= a^3 = (4.0\times 10^{-8})^3 = 6.4\times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3\).

61.solution: An ideal solution obeying Raoult's law over the whole range forms between components of nearly identical structure and intermolecular forces. Benzene + toluene is the classic ideal pair. Chloroform + acetone shows negative deviation (H-bonding), while carbon disulfide + acetone and ethanol + acetone show positive deviation.

62.subtopic: First-Order Kinetics, Rate Constant and Half-Life

63.solution: A ketone reacts with semicarbazide, \(\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{NH}-\text{CO}-\text{NH}_2\), to give a semicarbazone. So the reagent R is \(\text{NH}_2\text{NHCONH}_2\). Option A \((\text{NH}_2\text{OH})\) gives an oxime, option C (phenylhydrazine) gives a phenylhydrazone, and option D (hydrazine) gives a hydrazone.

64.solution: Polyacrylonitrile is made by free-radical (chain) addition polymerization of acrylonitrile, which is initiated by a peroxide (radical initiator). Nylon 6,6 and Bakelite are condensation polymers (no peroxide initiator needed).

65.subtopic: Position, Electronic Configuration and General Features of d-Block
65.solution: A transition element has partially filled d-orbitals in its atom or in a common ion. \(\text{Hg} = [\text{Xe}]4f^{14}5d^{10}6s^{2}\) has a completely filled \(d^{10}\) configuration (and \(\text{Hg}^{2+}\) is also \(d^{10}\)), so it is not regarded as a transition element. Ni, Fe and Ag have/form partially filled d-orbitals.

66.subtopic: Molar Conductivity, Kohlrausch's Law and Degree of Dissociation
66.solution: Molar conductivity \(\Lambda = \dfrac{1000\,k}{C}\), where \(k\) is conductivity and \(C\) is molarity. Rearranging gives \(k = \dfrac{\Lambda \times C}{1000}\), which is option A.

67.subtopic: Types of Solids, Crystal Systems and Properties
67.solution: Isotropic solids show the same value of a physical property (refractive index, conductivity, etc.) in all directions; this is characteristic of amorphous solids. Glass is amorphous and hence isotropic. Ceramics, graphite and ice are crystalline (anisotropic).

68.solution: \(\Delta S_{surr} = -\dfrac{\Delta H^{\circ}}{T} = -\dfrac{-208.6\times 10^{3}\ \text{J}}{298\ \text{K}} = +700\ \text{J K}^{-1}\). \(\Delta S_{total} = \Delta S_{sys} + \Delta S_{surr} = -36 + 700 = +664\ \text{J K}^{-1}\).

69.solution: A benzylic halide has the halogen on a carbon directly attached to a benzene ring. As printed, none of the options is a true benzylic halide: triphenylmethane has no halogen at all, 4-bromotoluene and bromobenzene are aryl halides, and 1-bromo-2-phenylethane \((\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br})\) is a homobenzylic (the Br is on the carbon beta to the ring). The intended answer is the triphenylmethyl (trityl) halide, mis-printed as 'triphenylmethane'. Keeping the official key A.
69.note: Flawed: option A 'Triphenylmethane' has no halogen; intended is triphenylmethyl halide (trityl, benzylic). No option as printed is a benzylic halide. Official key A retained as the intended answer.

70.subtopic: First-Order Kinetics, Rate Constant and Half-Life
70.solution: For a first-order reaction \(t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{k}\), which is independent of the initial concentration of the reactant. Doubling \([A]_0\) does not change \(t_{1/2}\); it remains the same.

71.solution: Both formaldehyde \((\text{HCHO})\) and benzaldehyde \((\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO})\) lack alpha-hydrogens, so with conc. \(\text{NaOH}\) they undergo a crossed Cannizzaro reaction. Formaldehyde, being the better reducing agent, is oxidised to methanoic acid (formic acid), while benzaldehyde is reduced to phenylmethanol (benzyl alcohol). Products: methanoic acid and phenylmethanol.
71.note: Option text 'Methanolic acid' is a mis-print for methanoic (formic) acid; the intended pair (methanoic acid + phenylmethanol) is correct.

72.solution: Water solubility depends on the ability to H-bond with water. The \(\text{O}-\text{H}\) bond of alcohols is more polar than the \(\text{N}-\text{H}\) bond of amines, so alcohols form stronger H-bonds; alkanes cannot H-bond at all. For compounds of comparable molar mass: alcohols \(>\) amines \(>\) alkanes.

73.solution: The ligand abbreviation 'en' stands for ethylenediamine \((\text{NH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2)\), a bidentate ligand. Only Bis(ethylenediamine)diisocyanato platinum(IV), \([\text{Pt(en)}_2(\text{NCO})_2]^{2+}\), contains 'en'.

74.solution: At STP, 1 mole of any ideal gas occupies \(22.4\ \text{dm}^3\). Therefore \(0.5\) mol \(\text{CO}_2\) occupies \(0.5 \times 22.4 = 11.2\ \text{dm}^3\).

75.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work
75.solution: Using \(\Delta U = Q + W\) (work-done-on-system convention). Work done on the system: \(W = +20\ \text{kJ}\). Heat released by the system: \(Q = -10\ \text{kJ}\). So \(\Delta U = -10 + 20 = +10\ \text{kJ}\).

76.subtopic: Group 1 Alkali Metals, Properties and Reactivity
76.solution: Lithium carbonate is the least stable group-1 carbonate (small \(\text{Li}^{+}\) polarises the carbonate) and decomposes on heating: \(\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Li}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2\). The products are \(\text{Li}_2\text{O}\) and \(\text{CO}_2\).

77.solution: In chlorobenzene, \(-\text{Cl}\) is an ortho/para director (it deactivates but directs o/p). Nitration with conc. \(\text{HNO}_3\) / conc. \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) gives a mixture of 1-chloro-2-nitrobenzene (ortho) and 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene (para). So the product is the o + p mixture.

78.solution: In the tetrathionate ion \(\text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-}\) \((^{-}\text{O}-\overset{1}{\text{S}}(=\!\text{O})_2-\overset{2}{\text{S}}-\overset{3}{\text{S}}-\overset{4}{\text{S}}(=\!\text{O})_2-\text{O}^{-})\): the two terminal sulphurs (1 and 4) are each bonded to three oxygens and one sulphur, giving oxidation state \(+5\); the two central sulphurs (2 and 3) are bonded only to sulphur (S-S bonds, like in a chain), giving oxidation state \(0\). The total \(2(+5) + 2(0) = +10\), balanced by \(6\times(-2)=-12\) for oxygen and net charge \(-2\). So \(+5, 0, 0, +5\).
78.note: Stem image (linear S4O6^2- structure with terminal S1, S4 bearing oxygens) read and confirmed.

79.solution: A primary allylic alcohol has \(-\text{OH}\) on a primary carbon that is also allylic (next to a \(\text{C}=\text{C}\)). Prop-2-en-1-ol (allyl alcohol), \(\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}\), is a primary allylic alcohol. Option A \((\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}-\text{CH(CH}_3)-\text{OH})\) is secondary, option C \((\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}-\text{C(CH}_3)_2-\text{OH})\) is tertiary, and option D \((\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH(CH}_3)-\text{OH})\) is secondary.
79.note: Options A, C, D are structure images (read); B is text. All four are allylic alcohols; B is the only primary one.

80.subtopic: Glycosidic Linkages in Di- and Polysaccharides
80.solution: Raffinose is a trisaccharide of galactose + glucose + fructose. Stachyose is a tetrasaccharide of two galactose units + glucose + fructose. Both contain galactose as a constituent. Sucrose (glucose+fructose), maltose (glucose+glucose) and lactose (galactose+glucose) do not both contain galactose.

81.subtopic: pH, pOH and Ionic Product of Water

82.solution: An \(MA_2BC\) octahedral/square-planar type has two identical ligands A plus two different ligands B and C, and shows geometric (cis-trans) diastereoisomerism. \([\text{Pt(NH}_3)(\text{H}_2\text{O})\text{Cl}_2]\) has A = Cl (two), B = \(\text{NH}_3\), C = \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\), i.e. \(MA_2BC\). Option A is \(M(\text{AA})_2B_2\), option C is \(MA_2B_2\), and option D is \(MA_4B_2\).

83.solution: Teflon (PTFE) is prepared by free-radical addition polymerization of tetrafluoroethene: \(n\,\text{CF}_2=\text{CF}_2 \to (\text{CF}_2-\text{CF}_2)_n\). Nylon 6, Nylon 6,6 and Perylene (Glyptal/condensation type) are made by condensation polymerization.

84.subtopic: Reactions of Alkenes, Addition, Oxidation and Ozonolysis
84.solution: Ozonolysis adds \(\text{O}_3\) across a \(\text{C}=\text{C}\) to give an ozonide, which on reductive cleavage (Zn/\(\text{H}_2\text{O}\)) gives carbonyl compounds. A \(=\!\text{CH}-\) carbon yields an aldehyde (and a \(=\!\text{CR}_2\) carbon yields a ketone). So one of the products is an aldehyde.

85.solution: Relative lowering of vapour pressure (dilute solution) \(= \dfrac{W_2 M_1}{W_1 M_2}\). So \(0.02 = \dfrac{20 \times 18}{200 \times M_2}\), giving \(M_2 = \dfrac{20 \times 18}{200 \times 0.02} = \dfrac{360}{4} = 90\ \text{g mol}^{-1}\).

86.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work
86.solution: Pressure-volume work for a gas reaction \(W = -\Delta n_g RT\), which is zero only when \(\Delta n_g = 0\). For \(\text{CH}_4(g) + \text{Cl}_2(g) \to \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}(g) + \text{HCl}(g)\), moles of gas: 2 reactant \(\to\) 2 product, \(\Delta n_g = 0\), so \(W = 0\). The other reactions have \(\Delta n_g \ne 0\).

87.subtopic: Preparation of Alkanes, Wurtz, Grignard and Decarboxylation
87.solution: Alkyl halide + Mg in dry ether gives the Grignard reagent \(\text{R}-\text{MgX}\) (A). The Grignard reagent reacts with a compound bearing an active hydrogen such as \(\text{NH}_3\): \(\text{R}-\text{MgX} + \text{NH}_3 \to \text{R}-\text{H} + \text{Mg(NH}_2)\text{X}\). The product B is the hydrocarbon (alkane) \(\text{R}-\text{H}\).

88.subtopic: Colloids, Classification, Coagulation and Hardy-Schulze Rule
88.solution: Match each process: (I) Dialysis is used for purification of a colloidal solution -> (D); (II) Peptization is preparation of a colloidal solution -> (C); (III) Emulsification underlies the cleansing action of soap -> (A); (IV) Electrophoresis (migration of colloidal particles) leads to coagulation at the electrode -> (B). Hence (I)-(D), (II)-(C), (III)-(A), (IV)-(B).

89.solution: An alcohol with molecular formula \(\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}\) is saturated and acyclic (degree of unsaturation = 0). Pentan-3-ol, \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\), is \(\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}\). Option A (cyclopentanol) is \(\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}\) (ring), option B (butan-1-ol) is \(\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}\) (only 4 carbons), and option D (cyclopent-3-en-1-ol) is \(\text{C}_5\text{H}_8\text{O}\) (ring + double bond).
89.note: All four options are structure images (read). Only C (pentan-3-ol) matches the saturated acyclic formula C5H12O.

90.subtopic: Gas Laws and Ideal Gas Equation
90.solution: From \(PV = nRT\) with equal \(V, T\): \(P \propto n = \dfrac{\text{mass}}{M}\). For equal masses, \(P \propto \dfrac{1}{M}\). Molar masses: \(\text{H}_2 (2) < \text{N}_2 (28) < \text{O}_2 (32) < \text{Cl}_2 (71)\). The gas of lowest molar mass, \(\text{H}_2\), gives the maximum pressure.

92.subtopic: Colour, Magnetic Properties and Spin-Only Formula
92.solution: Spin-only magnetic moment \(\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\,\text{BM}\) increases with the number of unpaired electrons \(n\). \(\text{V}^{3+}\) is \(3d^2\) (2 unpaired), \(\text{Cr}^{3+}\) is \(3d^3\) (3), \(\text{Mn}^{2+}\) is \(3d^5\) (5), \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\) is \(3d^6\) (4). \(\text{V}^{3+}\) has the fewest unpaired electrons, hence the lowest magnetic moment.

93.solution: At the anode: \(2\text{Cl}^{-} \to \text{Cl}_2 + 2e^{-}\), so 1 mol \(\text{Cl}_2\) needs 2 mol electrons \((2\times 96500\ \text{C})\). For 0.5 mol \(\text{Cl}_2\), charge \(Q = 0.5\times 2\times 96500 = 96500\ \text{C}\). With \(I = 100\ \text{A}\), \(t = \dfrac{Q}{I} = \dfrac{96500}{100} = 965\ \text{s}\).

94.solution: Number of unit cells in \(x\) g \(= \dfrac{x}{\rho a^3}\); for bcc each cell has \(n=2\) atoms, so number of atoms \(= \dfrac{x\,n}{\rho a^3}\). With \(x = 1.58\) g, \(\rho a^3 = 1.58\times 10^{-22}\) g: atoms \(= \dfrac{1.58 \times 2}{1.58\times 10^{-22}} = 2.0\times 10^{22}\).

95.subtopic: Group 16 Chalcogens, Oxygen, Sulphur and Ozone
95.solution: Thermal stability of group-16 hydrides decreases down the group as the \(\text{E}-\text{H}\) bond strength falls: \(\text{H}_2\text{O} > \text{H}_2\text{S} > \text{H}_2\text{Se} > \text{H}_2\text{Te}\). Written as increasing order this is \(\text{H}_2\text{Te} < \text{H}_2\text{Se} < \text{H}_2\text{S} < \text{H}_2\text{O}\).

96.solution: Longest wavelength = smallest energy gap. For the Lyman series \(n_1 = 1\); the smallest gap is the \(n_2=2 \to n_1=1\) transition. \(\bar{\nu} = R_H\left(\dfrac{1}{1^2} - \dfrac{1}{2^2}\right) = 109677 \times \dfrac{3}{4} = 82257.75\ \text{cm}^{-1}\). So \(\lambda = \dfrac{1}{\bar{\nu}} = \dfrac{4}{3\times 109677} = 1.216\times 10^{-5}\ \text{cm}\).

97.subtopic: IUPAC and Common Nomenclature of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
97.solution: Pyrogallol is the 1,2,3-trihydroxybenzene, so its IUPAC name is benzene-1,2,3-triol. (Benzene-1,3,5-triol is phloroglucinol; benzene-1,3-diol is resorcinol; benzene-1,4-diol is hydroquinone.)

98.subtopic: Green Chemistry, Principles, Atom Economy and Green Solvents
98.solution: \(\%\ \text{atom economy} = \dfrac{\text{formula weight of desired product}}{\text{sum of formula weights of all reactants}} \times 100\). So formula weight of product \(= \dfrac{\%\,\text{atom economy} \times \text{sum of reactant FW}}{100} = \dfrac{50 \times 274}{100} = 137\ \text{u}\).

99.solution: A salt of a strong acid and a strong base does not hydrolyse (its ions do not react with water). \(\text{KNO}_3\) (from \(\text{HNO}_3\) + \(\text{KOH}\)) is such a salt and is not hydrolysed. \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\) and \(\text{KCN}\) (salts of weak acid) and \(\text{NH}_4\text{CN}\) (weak acid + weak base) all undergo hydrolysis.

100.solution: By Saytzeff's rule, dehydrohalogenation preferentially gives the more substituted (more stable) alkene, which has the greatest number of alkyl groups on the doubly bonded carbons. The tetrasubstituted alkene \(\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{CR}_2\) is the most stable and is therefore formed most easily.
